l4_steps.name: Compile CAMO annual audit programme
l4_steps.input: Regulatory calendar (EASA Part-CAMO / FAR Part 145), contracted MRO provider list, prior audit cycle dates
l4_steps.output: Approved annual audit schedule with provider assignments and due dates
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Part-145 approved providers audited within 24-month cycle; schedule published ≥60 days before Q1
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO provider network spans 15+ stations; manual calendar alignment in spreadsheets leads to audit gaps when contracts are added mid-year without AMOS notification trigger

l4_steps.name: Risk-score providers using performance data
l4_steps.input: Historical finding rates, open CAR age, repeat finding history, on-time delivery metrics from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Provider risk ranking matrix (High / Medium / Low) with scoring rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Risk model refresh completed ≤5 business days after each completed audit; High-risk providers flagged within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Reliability data is siloed across AMOS and airline OTP systems; manual data extraction introduces 1–2 week lag that distorts risk scores

l4_steps.name: Determine if expedited audit is required
l4_steps.input: Provider risk score, occurrence reports filed against provider, regulatory authority safety bulletins
l4_steps.output: Audit priority decision: standard schedule maintained or expedited audit triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Expedited audit commenced within 10 business days of trigger event; 0 High-risk providers left unaudited >6 months
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA/FAA safety bulletins arrive via email with no automated AMOS integration; manual triage by QA Manager creates response-time variability

l4_steps.name: Retrieve prior audit findings and open CARs
l4_steps.input: Provider ID, audit history reference, open Corrective Action Request (CAR) log
l4_steps.output: Prior finding summary report with CAR status (open / overdue / closed)
l4_steps.kpi: CAR retrieval completed within 1 business day; zero open Level 1 CARs permitted before new audit commences
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy AMOS implementations store CAR evidence as unstructured PDF attachments; keyword search across >500 CARs per provider is unreliable without structured data entry discipline

l4_steps.name: Generate compliance checklist from Part-145 requirements
l4_steps.input: EASA Part-145 / FAR 145 regulatory requirements, airline-specific MOE (Maintenance Organisation Exposition), prior non-conformances
l4_steps.output: Structured audit checklist with regulatory reference codes and prior finding flags
l4_steps.kpi: Checklist covers 100% of applicable regulatory subparts; prior repeat-finding items tagged for enhanced scrutiny
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA AMC amendments (e.g. 2022 Part-CAMO revision) require manual checklist updates; no automated regulatory change management feed into AMOS checklist library

l4_steps.name: Issue formal pre-audit notification to provider
l4_steps.input: Approved audit schedule, checklist scope, lead auditor assignment
l4_steps.output: Pre-audit notification letter with scope, dates, document request list transmitted to Part-145 provider
l4_steps.kpi: Notification issued ≥14 calendar days before audit start; document request acknowledgement received within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Some third-party MRO stations (particularly overseas line stations) acknowledge notifications informally via WhatsApp rather than through AMOS supplier portal, creating audit-trail gaps

l4_steps.name: Confirm provider readiness and document receipt
l4_steps.input: Pre-audit document submission from provider (MOE, personnel licences, equipment calibration records, training records)
l4_steps.output: Readiness confirmation or audit postponement decision
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of requested documents received and reviewed before audit day 1; postponement rate <10% of scheduled audits
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS document portal upload limits (50 MB per file) cause providers to split calibration certificate packages across multiple uploads, increasing pre-audit review time by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Conduct opening meeting and confirm audit scope
l4_steps.input: Audit checklist, attendee list (provider Accountable Manager, QA lead, production planning), pre-audit findings
l4_steps.output: Signed scope-confirmation record; audit log opened in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Opening meeting completed within 1 hour; scope agreed and documented before hangar/records access begins
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote line stations (e.g. outstation MRO) conduct opening meetings via video call; AMOS audit log does not capture video-session metadata, creating traceability gaps for regulatory inspectors

l4_steps.name: Audit technical records for airworthiness compliance
l4_steps.input: Aircraft technical logbooks, Airworthiness Directive (AD) compliance records, component removal/installation logs, deferred defect register
l4_steps.output: Records audit worksheet with compliance status per AD/SB and identified discrepancies
l4_steps.kpi: AD compliance rate ≥99.5% across sampled aircraft tail numbers; zero unaddressed mandatory ADs permitted
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP airworthiness data is not always synchronised with provider's AMOS work-order records in real time; delta between systems causes false AD non-compliance flags requiring manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Inspect maintenance facilities, tooling, and personnel
l4_steps.input: Tooling calibration register, Part-66 licence currency list, hangar environment records (FOD control logs, lighting/temperature)
l4_steps.output: Facilities inspection record with pass/fail status per checklist item
l4_steps.kpi: Tooling calibration current for ≥99% of items sampled; zero expired Part-66 licences on active maintenance staff
l4_steps.pain_point: Calibration certificates managed in provider's local spreadsheet rather than AMOS; discrepancies between paper records and AMOS calibration register are a recurring Level 2 finding

l4_steps.name: Classify findings and identify Level 1 safety issues
l4_steps.input: Completed audit checklist, records worksheet, facilities inspection record
l4_steps.output: Preliminary finding classification (Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3) entered in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: All findings classified within 4 hours of audit completion; Level 1 findings notified to Accountable Manager within 2 hours of identification
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA Level 1 / Level 2 classification criteria have grey areas (e.g. incomplete but not falsified records); inconsistent classification between auditors increases provider dispute rate and regulatory risk

l4_steps.name: Issue stop-work notice or immediate CAR for Level 1
l4_steps.input: Level 1 finding record, regulatory authority contact details, affected aircraft tail numbers
l4_steps.output: Formal stop-work notice or immediate CAR issued; regulatory authority notified within 24 hours per EASA Part-CAMO M.B.902
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory authority notification within 24 hours of Level 1 finding; stop-work enforced within 2 hours on affected task
l4_steps.pain_point: Stop-work authority at outstations requires on-call Accountable Manager approval; out-of-hours time-zone issues cause average 4-hour delay in Level 1 stop-work enforcement at overseas stations

l4_steps.name: Finalise audit report and issue CARs to provider
l4_steps.input: Classified finding list, provider Accountable Manager details, regulatory references per finding
l4_steps.output: Signed audit report and numbered CARs issued to provider within 5 business days of audit close
l4_steps.kpi: Audit report issued within 5 business days; CAR numbering 100% traceable to audit report section
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS CAR module does not auto-populate regulatory reference citations; auditors manually copy EASA AMC text, introducing transcription errors that providers use to dispute finding validity

l4_steps.name: Review and accept or reject provider CAP response
l4_steps.input: Provider Corrective Action Plan (CAP) with root-cause analysis, containment action, corrective action, preventive action, and target completion dates
l4_steps.output: CAP acceptance or rejection with specific deficiency comments returned to provider
l4_steps.kpi: CAP response received from provider within 10 business days (Level 1) / 30 days (Level 2); first-submission acceptance rate ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Providers frequently submit '5-Why' root-cause analyses that misidentify systemic causes as individual errors, leading to repeat findings in subsequent audits; AMOS has no CAP quality scoring mechanism

l4_steps.name: Track CAP implementation and verify closure evidence
l4_steps.input: Accepted CAP with milestone dates, provider evidence submissions (revised procedures, training records, calibration certificates)
l4_steps.output: CAR closure record with verified evidence reference; overdue CARs escalated to Accountable Manager
l4_steps.kpi: CAR on-time closure rate ≥90%; zero Level 1 CARs open beyond 30 days; Level 2 CARs closed within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS CAR closure workflow requires Accountable Manager digital signature but does not enforce two-person review; single-reviewer closure of Level 1 CARs has been flagged in EASA SAFA audits as a systemic gap

l4_steps.name: Monitor fleet-wide AD and SB compliance status
l4_steps.input: FAA/EASA AD feeds, Boeing Service Bulletin library, current aircraft maintenance status from AMOS
l4_steps.output: AD/SB compliance dashboard with next-due dates and overdue alerts by tail number
l4_steps.kpi: AD compliance rate ≥99.9% at fleet level; zero aircraft operated with overdue mandatory ADs; SB incorporation decisions documented within 30 days of issue
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP receives FAA AD feeds automatically but EASA ADs require manual import from EASA e-Rules portal; 24–72 hour lag creates window where a newly effective EASA AD is not yet reflected in CAMP, risking inadvertent non-compliance

l4_steps.name: Analyse reliability programme outputs for adverse trends
l4_steps.input: PIREP/MAREP data from AMOS, component removal rates, in-flight shutdown rates, delay/cancellation codes, industry benchmark data (IATA MCTM)
l4_steps.output: Monthly reliability report with control chart trend analysis and alert flag list
l4_steps.kpi: Reliability report published by 5th working day of each month; alert threshold breach investigated within 10 business days; IFSD rate ≤0.02 per 1,000 engine hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay/cancellation codes entered by operations staff often misclassify maintenance-caused events as ATC or weather; data quality issues in AMOS cause reliability metrics to undercount maintenance-driven disruptions

l4_steps.name: Submit mandatory occurrence reports to regulator
l4_steps.system: ECCAIRS 2 (European Coordination Centre for Accident and Incident Reporting Systems)
l4_steps.input: Occurrence reports from maintenance crews, AMOS defect records, CAMO safety investigation findings
l4_steps.output: Mandatory occurrence report (MOR) submitted to EASA / national CAA within 72 hours per Regulation (EU) 376/2014; ASRS report filed for US operations
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of reportable occurrences submitted within 72-hour regulatory deadline; MOR rejection rate <2%; follow-up investigation reports submitted within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy (≥1,800 occurrence categories) is complex; front-line reporters default to generic codes, reducing data quality for safety trend analysis across the European aviation safety database
